observation.visible_scene: A close-up studio shot of three faceted gemstones arranged in a loose triangle on a glossy, light-blue reflective surface: a blue gem (upper area), a pink/magenta gem (lower-left initially), and a pale lavender/clear gem (right). The background contains large, out-of-focus gem shapes (blue on the left edge, red on the right edge, clear at top) that act as blurred reflections/bokeh. Bright star-shaped lens-flare sparkles appear on the facets. Heavy chromatic (red/cyan) fringing is visible along edges throughout.
visible_changes: The viewpoint slowly orbits/rotates around the gem cluster: over the excerpt the triangle of gems turns counter-clockwise in image space, so the blue gem drifts from top toward the left, the lavender gem from right toward top-center, and the pink gem from lower-left toward lower-right.

Each gem's apparent orientation changes continuously (side profiles gradually give way to more top-down views showing round girdle/table facets), consistent with camera orbit and/or slow gem rotation.
The framing tightens slightly (mild zoom-in) and tilts toward a top-down angle, making the pink gem read as a round oval and the blue gem as a round brilliant by the end.
Star-flare sparkles flicker on and off across different facets of the pink and lavender gems frame to frame.
The blurred background gems shift shape and position (parallax), and the on-surface reflections of the three gems move in step with them.
The chromatic-aberration fringing at the image edges varies in intensity between frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rotation is camera orbit, object spin, or both, and what drives it (no operator or mechanism visible).
The full arrangement of gems and the surface beyond the blurred background; the state before t=0 and after the last frame.
Whether the motion is a continuous loop or part of a longer sequence with cuts.
uncertain_details: Exact 3D positions and identities of the background blurred gems (reflections vs. separate objects is not fully resolvable).
Whether individual gems rotate on their own axes or only appear to turn due to camera motion.
The cause of the sparkle flashes (rendered lens effect vs. physical light source).
